This report defines a **reference counterfactual** for the preferential sampling bias and estimates
it. The construction is: hold the field year fixed, and ask what sampling bias that field would have
suffered had the array been advected by a *different* year's circulation. Averaging that over every
unaligned circulation gives a reference; the aligned circulation's bias minus that reference is the
estimand. Nothing is held out for validation and nothing is refit — the name that suggests otherwise
is deliberately avoided.

It reads the design ensembles produced and described in
[Monte-Carlo Sampling Distributions of the Residual-Field Mean](mean_estimation_mc.html), which is
the prerequisite: the analysis measure $\mathbb{P}$, the truth $\bar Z_k$, the residual field
$\tilde Z_k$, the two analysis boxes, and the per-cell bias
$B_k^{(l,d)} = \hat Z^{(l,d)}_k - \bar Z_k$ are all defined and measured there. In brief,
$B_k^{(l,d)}$ is the bias incurred when floats advected by velocity year $l$ under deployment
replicate $d$ sample the residual OHC field of analysis year $k$; there are $M = 10$ velocity years,
$m = 10$ analysis years, and $D = 750$ deployment replicates per velocity year, in each of two boxes.

**What is new here, and what is not.** That report's §7 forms a *gapped* contrast $T_k$ — the aligned
cell against the flows at $|l-k| \ge 2$ — and identifies it with preferential sampling under an
assumption (P). The construction below differs in three ways.

1. The target is defined **first, as a functional of the realised record**, and the estimator is then
   shown to be exactly unbiased for it — with no assumption on the velocity fields, the residual
   fields, or their relationship. Assumption (P) is not required to *identify* $\Theta_k$; it is
   required only to call $\Theta_k$ preferential sampling. That is a real gain in rigour, and it is
   also less of a gain than it first appears: see @sec-caveats.
2. The reference uses **every** unaligned flow, $l \ne k$, not a gapped subset. The gap becomes a
   sensitivity analysis rather than part of the definition.
3. The variance is exact rather than approximated by an across-year spread, including for the pooled
   estimate, and the full covariance across analysis years is available — which is what makes the
   drift statement in @sec-drift possible at all.

The numbers are not new. The two estimands differ by the known factor $\tfrac{M-1}{M}$
(@sec-relation), so this report *reframes and re-errors* quantities the companion already reported;
it does not overturn them. The companion's hypothesis test is treated separately in
[A Permutation Test for Preferential Sampling](permutation_test.html).

# The estimand

## Setup

The velocity fields $\tilde V_1,\dots,\tilde V_M$ and residual fields $\tilde Z_1,\dots,\tilde Z_M$
are **fixed**: they are realised reanalysis output, and no distribution is placed over them. All
randomness enters through the deployment draws $\omega_{l,d} \overset{iid}{\sim} \mathcal{D}$, and
every expectation and variance below is with respect to $\mathcal{D}$ alone, conditional on the
realised fields.

For a design $X = \{x_1,\dots,x_n\} \subset \mathcal{X}$ write

$$\mu_X \;:=\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}_X - \mathbb{P}, \qquad
\hat{\mathbb{P}}_X \;=\; \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \delta_{x_i},$$

a signed measure of total mass zero on $\mathcal{X}$, whose restriction to the analysis partition
$\{c_j\}_{j=1}^C$ is the vector $(w_1 - p_1,\dots,w_C - p_C)$. Because $\tilde Z_k$ is constant
within cells, the bias is *exactly* the bilinear pairing

$$B_k(X) \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mu_X \;=\; \langle \mu_X, \tilde Z_k\rangle
\;=\; \sum_{j=1}^C (w_j - p_j)\,\tilde Z_{k,j},$$

an identity rather than an approximation: $\tilde Z_k$ is a bounded simple function and $\mu_X$ a
finite signed measure. Abbreviate $\mu^{(l,d)} := \mu_{X^{(l,d)}}$ and
$B_k^{(l,d)} := \langle \mu^{(l,d)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$.

The object the construction is built on is the **mean footprint** of a velocity year,

$$m^{(l)} \;:=\; \mathbb{E}_{\omega\sim\mathcal{D}}\big[\mu_{\mathcal{G}(\omega,\,\tilde V_l)}\big],$$

the deployment-averaged design deviation induced by flow year $l$. Since $\mathcal{D}$ and
$\tilde V_l$ are fixed, $m^{(l)}$ is a deterministic zero-mass signed measure; existence is immediate
because $w_j \in [0,1]$ and $C < \infty$, so $\mu^{(l,d)}$ is uniformly bounded.

## The reference counterfactual

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
For an analysis year $k$, the **unaligned reference footprint** is

$$\bar m^{(-k)} \;:=\; \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l \ne k} m^{(l)},$$

and the **alignment contrast** is

$$\Theta_k \;:=\; \big\langle\, m^{(k)} - \bar m^{(-k)},\;\; \tilde Z_k \,\big\rangle .$$
:::

In words: the excess sampling bias against field year $k$ produced by that year's own circulation,
relative to the bias the remaining $M-1$ circulations would have produced against the *same* field.
Both terms are deterministic, so $\Theta_k$ is a **fixed quantity attached to the realised record**,
in the units of $\tilde Z$ (J m$^{-2}$) — not a parameter of a population of oceans.

**Coverage bias cancels identically.** Write $m^{(l)} = \bar m + \delta^{(l)}$, with $\bar m$
collecting whatever is shared by every flow year — the array's persistent non-uniformity from
deployment geography, the time-mean circulation, and bathymetry — and $\delta^{(l)}$ the departure
induced by year $l$'s eddy field. Then

$$\Theta_k \;=\; \big\langle (\bar m + \delta^{(k)}) - (\bar m + \bar\delta^{(-k)}),\; \tilde Z_k\big\rangle
\;=\; \big\langle \delta^{(k)} - \bar\delta^{(-k)},\; \tilde Z_k\big\rangle,$$

so $\bar m$ drops out. The cancellation follows from linearity alone and holds for *any*
decomposition of that form: a quantity not varying with $l$ cannot survive a difference taken across
$l$. The structure responsible is that $\Theta_k$ differences two **designs** against a **single**
field. Had the comparison held the design fixed and varied the field, as in
$\langle m^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k - \tilde Z_{k'}\rangle$, the common footprint would multiply
$\tilde Z_k - \tilde Z_{k'} \ne 0$ and would not cancel. Holding the field fixed while varying the
circulation is the load-bearing feature, not an incidental choice.

The excluded term $\langle \bar m, \tilde Z_k\rangle$ is the **coverage bias**. It is typically the
larger of the two contributions to the total $\langle m^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$, and it is excluded
deliberately: coverage bias is a deterministic function of position and can be computed and removed
given the profile locations and a climatology, or suppressed by inverse-intensity weighting.
Preferential bias admits no such correction — it is a covariance between the design and the component
of the field that position does not predict, so reweighting by position cannot reach it. The two
differ in kind, not merely in magnitude.

**Why the reference excludes $k$.** The alternative is to centre on the grand mean
$\bar m = M^{-1}\sum_l m^{(l)}$. That is less convenient because $\sum_l (m^{(l)} - \bar m) = 0$
forces the reference to depend on year $k$ itself: any excess in $m^{(k)}$ is offset by a
compensating deficit spread across the remaining years, so a contrast against a strict subset of them
acquires a multiplicative distortion and a residual depending on which years were excluded. Removing
$k$ from its own reference eliminates the constraint. The two differ by a known factor,
$\langle m^{(k)} - \bar m, \tilde Z_k\rangle = \tfrac{M-1}{M}\Theta_k$, verified numerically in
@tbl-audit.

# The estimator

Let $\bar G_{kl} := D^{-1}\sum_{d=1}^D B_k^{(l,d)}$ be the cell mean of the simulation array — the
heatmap of the companion report, read one row at a time.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
$$\widehat\Theta_k \;:=\; \bar G_{kk} \;-\; \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l \ne k} \bar G_{kl}.$$
:::

**Exact unbiasedness.** $\mathbb{E}[\widehat\Theta_k] = \Theta_k$ for every $k$. Each $\mu^{(l,d)}$
is bounded and $C < \infty$, so $B_k^{(l,d)}$ is integrable and expectation commutes with the finite
sums. By linearity of the pairing in its first argument, and because the $\omega_{l,d}$ are
identically distributed across $d$,

$$\mathbb{E}\big[\bar G_{kl}\big] \;=\; \frac1D \sum_d \big\langle \mathbb{E}[\mu^{(l,d)}], \tilde Z_k\big\rangle
\;=\; \big\langle m^{(l)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle,$$

and applying linearity once more to the definition gives $\Theta_k$.

The proof uses only linearity of the pairing, boundedness, and identical distribution of deployment
draws *within* a cell. It does **not** require the designs to be identically distributed across
velocity years, the residual fields to be exchangeable, or any distributional form for $B$. Those are
what it takes to attach a $p$-value, not to estimate $\Theta_k$. Estimation and inference are
therefore separable, which matters here because the companion permutation-test report finds two of
the four randomisation assumptions rejected by the data: $\widehat\Theta_k$ can be reported with a
standard error even where the randomisation hypothesis is in doubt.

# Variance

Write $\sigma^2_{kl} := \operatorname{Var}_{\omega\sim\mathcal{D}}\big(\langle
\mu_{\mathcal{G}(\omega,\tilde V_l)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle\big)$, the deployment variance of the
single-design bias in cell $(k,l)$, again finite by boundedness. If the deployment draws are mutually
independent across all pairs $(l,d)$ — which this OSSE satisfies, since every velocity year is seeded
from its own draw and no common random numbers are used — the cell means $\{\bar G_{kl}\}_l$ are
independent and

$$\operatorname{Var}\big(\widehat\Theta_k\big) \;=\; \frac1D\left[\sigma^2_{kk}
+ \frac{1}{(M-1)^2}\sum_{l\ne k}\sigma^2_{kl}\right].
$$ {#eq-var}

$\sigma^2_{kl}$ is estimated by the within-cell sample variance of $\{B_k^{(l,d)}\}_{d}$, which
requires no model. It is worth noting what it is *not*: for $n$ independent draws from $\mathbb{P}$
one would have $\sigma^2_{kl} = \operatorname{Var}_\mathbb{P}(\tilde Z_k)\,\mathbb{E}[1/n]$, but
advected floats are strongly clustered along trajectories, so consecutive profiles are near-replicates
and the effective sample size is far below $n$. The empirical within-cell variance captures this
automatically; the companion report measures the float-clustered design effect at $\approx 1.8$.

## The homoscedastic reduction should not be used

If $\sigma^2_{kl} \equiv \sigma^2_k$ for all $l$, @eq-var collapses to
$\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + (M-1)^{-1})$. That reduction is tempting because it is the form in which the
variance is comparable to a gapped contrast's, but it is not satisfied here.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-var
#| echo: false

HTML(fmt(mm.alignment_variance_table(), 4))
```

: How far $\sigma^2_{kl}$ is from constant in $l$, and what assuming otherwise costs. The first
column is the median over $k$ of $\max_l \sigma^2_{kl} / \min_l \sigma^2_{kl}$; the last two compare
the standard error from @eq-var against the homoscedastic reduction, averaged over analysis years.
{#tbl-var}

The within-row spread of $\sigma^2_{kl}$ is a factor of $1.8$ in Box B and $1.5$ in Box A, driven by
genuinely different retention across flow years — a year that holds more floats inside the box yields
a larger $n$ and a tighter $\hat Z$. The *consequence* for the standard error is small ($1.9\%$ and
$1.1\%$), because the reduction misstates only the reference term, which carries weight
$(M-1)^{-2} = 1/81$. Everything below nonetheless uses @eq-var: the reduction buys nothing and its
premise is false as measured.

## The pooled variance in closed form

The pooled estimand is $\bar\Theta := m^{-1}\sum_k \Theta_k$, and unbiasedness of
$\widehat{\bar\Theta} := m^{-1}\sum_k \widehat\Theta_k$ is immediate by linearity. Its variance does
*not* factorise, because $\widehat\Theta_k$ and $\widehat\Theta_{k'}$ are built from the same
simulations. A worst-case bound $\max_k \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\Theta_k)$ is available but is very
loose — here it overstates the standard error by $3.4\times$ (Box B) and $3.8\times$ (Box A).

The exact variance is available in closed form and no resampling is needed. Let
$c_{kl} = \mathbb{1}\{k = l\} - \mathbb{1}\{k \ne l\}/(M-1)$ be the contrast weights, and define the
per-draw unit statistic

$$U^{(l,d)} \;:=\; \frac1m \sum_k c_{kl}\, B_k^{(l,d)},
\qquad\text{so that}\qquad
\widehat{\bar\Theta} \;=\; \sum_l \frac{1}{D_l}\sum_d U^{(l,d)} .$$

The $U^{(l,d)}$ are independent across $(l,d)$ — every dependence among the $\widehat\Theta_k$ enters
through their sharing a *draw*, which the reindexing collects into a single scalar — so

$$\operatorname{Var}\big(\widehat{\bar\Theta}\big) \;=\; \sum_l \frac{\operatorname{Var}_d\big(U^{(l,\cdot)}\big)}{D_l}
\;=\; \frac{\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma\, \mathbf{1}}{m^2},$$

with $\Sigma$ the exact covariance matrix of $\{\widehat\Theta_k\}$, assembled the same way. Both
routes are computed and agreed in @tbl-audit. The same $\Sigma$ is what @sec-drift needs.

Empirically the off-diagonal correlations of $\Sigma$ are tiny — mean $+0.006$, range $-0.03$ to
$+0.04$ in both boxes — so pooling gains almost the full $\sqrt{m}$. That is a *measurement*, not an
assumption: the estimator's weights are the only coupling, and they are small relative to the
deployment noise at $D = 750$.

**Box B: all ten years negative.** $\widehat\Theta_k$ runs from $-0.101$ to $-0.027$ GJ/m$^2$,
$-1.9$ to $-8.4$ standard errors from zero, with no year of the opposite sign. Standardized, that is
$-0.004$ to $-0.015\,\sigma_k$. The sign is what an advective array should produce if floats
preferentially occupy anomalously cool water relative to the analysis measure, or equivalently if the
warm anomalies of a given year are the ones the array under-visits.

**Box A: small, mixed, and not zero.** Individual years run $-0.009$ to $+0.012$ GJ/m$^2$, six
positive and four negative, and only four exceed two standard errors in absolute value. This is the subtropical-gyre
control, and at the per-year level it behaves like one.

- **Box A's pooled level is not zero.** It is $20\times$ smaller than Box B's and of the opposite
  sign, but the Monte Carlo resolves it. Box A is a *weak-and-opposite* control, not a null one. This
  is a sharpening of the companion report's reading, and it comes entirely from the exact pooled
  standard error: the across-year standard error used there is $0.0019$ GJ/m$^2$ on a contrast $0.9\times$
  the size of this one, i.e. $0.0021$ in $\Theta$ units — nearly twice as wide, because it inherits
  the between-year spread, which is real structure and not estimation error.
- **Most of the across-year spread is real.** In Box B the observed across-year sd is $0.0265$
  GJ/m$^2$ against a Monte Carlo part of $0.0126$, leaving a between-year sd of $0.0233$ — so year to
  year, $\Theta_k$ genuinely moves by about a third of its own pooled magnitude. The same is true in
  Box A ($0.0056$ against $0.0036$). $\Theta_k$ is a per-year quantity with per-year structure, not a
  constant measured ten times.

## Temporal coverage versus spatial concentration

: $\widehat\Theta_k$ split into its day-of-year-marginal component and the spatial remainder, both
boxes, in GJ/m$^2$. The temporal term is computed in closed form from the domain mean's day-of-year
series, not by simulation. {#tbl-decomp}

The contrast is **spatial to within one per cent**. Box B's pooled $-0.0655$ is $+0.0007$ temporal and
$-0.0663$ spatial; Box A's $+0.0033$ is $+0.0003$ and $+0.0030$. This is the expected result and it is
worth saying why: the day-of-year ramp is a property of the release schedule, identical across flow
years, so it sits almost entirely in $\bar m$ and cancels in a difference taken along $l$. It does
*not* cancel from the aligned bias itself, where the companion report measures it carrying an r.m.s.
of $0.036$ GJ/m$^2$. The cancellation is a property of the construction, and this table is the check
that it happened.

# Drift, not level {#sec-drift}

A preferential offset constant in time affects the estimated mean state but **cancels in anomalies
and trends**, which are the quantities used in ocean-heat-uptake and Earth-energy-imbalance
assessments. A *time-varying* offset does not. Since the real Argo array roughly tripled between 2004
and 2007, standardised parking depths, changed float models, and expanded to high latitudes, any
accompanying change in trapping propensity appears as a spurious heat flux. Estimating $\Theta_k$
separately by year is therefore the more informative use of the construction, and the exact covariance
$\Sigma$ makes the drift a well-posed generalized-least-squares problem rather than an ordinary
regression on correlated points.

Writing $b$ for the GLS slope of $\{\widehat\Theta_k\}$ on year, the implied flux is
$10b / (3.1536\times10^8)$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade, the denominator being seconds per decade.

**The two boxes separate on exactly this axis**, and in the opposite direction to the levels.

- **Box B** has a large level and **no drift**: $b = -0.0001 \pm 0.0013$ GJ/m$^2$/yr, $t = -0.07$,
  i.e. $-0.003$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade. Over these ten years its preferential bias is a stable offset.
- **Box A** has a level near zero and **a drift resolved at $t = +4.3$**: $b = +0.0018 \pm 0.0004$
  GJ/m$^2$/yr, or $+0.056$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade against a present energy imbalance of order
  $0.8$ W m$^{-2}$.

Read carefully, this is the more consequential of the two findings, and it inverts the naive reading
of @tbl-theta: the box whose pooled contrast looks like a null control is the one whose contrast is
*moving*. Three qualifications belong immediately with it, and are not optional.

1. **The drift is descriptive of these ten years.** It is a least-squares summary of ten correlated
   numbers attached to a realised record, not an inference to a population of years. The standard
   error is the Monte Carlo error of the ten $\widehat\Theta_k$; it does not include, and cannot
   include, the variability of the ocean state that generated them. There is one realisation of each
   year.
2. **A ten-year window cannot separate trend from low-frequency variability.** Gyre state and the
   North Atlantic Oscillation have decadal timescales, so a monotone $\Theta_k$ over 2010--2019 is
   equally consistent with one phase of an oscillation.
3. **The mechanism here is not the mechanism of concern.** The real-Argo drift threat is a *changing
   array* — more floats, different parking, new regions. This OSSE holds the deployment law fixed by
   construction and varies only the flow, so what it measures is drift in the flow--field coupling,
   which is a different thing and a lower bound on nothing in particular. The OSSE demonstrates that
   the quantity is estimable and moves; it does not estimate the historical Argo drift.

# Relation to the gapped contrast {#sec-relation}

The companion report's statistic is $T_k = \bar G_{kk} - |\mathcal{C}_k|^{-1}\sum_{l\in\mathcal{C}_k}
\bar G_{kl}$ with $\mathcal{C}_k = \{l : |l-k| \ge 2\}$, and its per-year table is centred on the
*grand* column mean. Two comparisons matter.

**The grand-mean version is $\Theta_k$ up to a known factor.** Centring on $\bar m$ rather than
$\bar m^{(-k)}$ gives exactly $\tfrac{M-1}{M}\Theta_k = 0.9\,\Theta_k$ here; the pooled $-0.0590$ and
$+0.0030$ GJ/m$^2$ of the companion's contrast table are $0.9$ times the $-0.0655$ and $+0.0033$
above, to machine precision (@tbl-audit). **This report changes the framing and the error bars, not
the measurement.** That is worth stating plainly, because "an unbiased estimator with no assumptions"
could otherwise be read as a claim to have measured something the earlier analysis could not.

**The variance advantage over a gapped contrast is real and immaterial.** Under the homoscedastic
model a gapped contrast with $c = |\mathcal{C}_k| < M-1$ has variance $\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + c^{-1})$
against $\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + (M-1)^{-1})$, so the full reference is strictly tighter. With
$M = 10$ and $c$ typically $8$, the ratio of standard errors is about $1.006$ — six parts in a
thousand. The case for the full reference is that it defines a clean estimand, not that it is more
efficient. Any claim resting on the efficiency gain should be dropped.

# Is the reference contaminated? {#sec-contamination}

The reference $\bar m^{(-k)}$ includes the adjacent years $l = k \pm 1$, whose circulations retain
dependence on $\tilde Z_k$ through ocean memory. If such residual alignment exists it inflates the
reference toward the aligned cell and shrinks $\Theta_k$ — which is why the companion report imposes
the $|l-k| \ge 2$ gap in the first place. The gap is not needed here to *define* $\Theta_k$, so the
question becomes a measurement.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-contam
#| echo: false

HTML(fmt(mm.alignment_contamination_table(), 4))
```

: Left block: the mean deviation of a reference cell from its own analysis year's row mean, split by
whether the flow is one year off or two or more, in GJ/m$^2$, with the difference and its standard
error. Right block: pooled $\widehat{\bar\Theta}$ with the full reference against a reference
restricted to $|l-k| \ge 2$, and their ratio. The restricted version is a *different estimand*, shown
only to size the effect. {#tbl-contam}

**There is no evidence of memory contamination, and what evidence there is has the wrong sign.** In
Box B the lag-$1$ reference cells sit $+0.0051 \pm 0.0073$ GJ/m$^2$ above the lag-$\ge 2$ cells
($t = 0.70$); in Box A, $-0.0015 \pm 0.0016$ ($t = -0.90$). Neither is distinguishable from zero.
More tellingly, the aligned cells in Box B deviate by $-0.059$ GJ/m$^2$ — strongly *negative* — while
the lag-$1$ cells deviate *positively*. Contamination by ocean memory would put lag-$1$ cells on the
same side as lag $0$ and have them decay toward zero with distance; the lag profile in the companion
report shows instead a spike at lag $0$ and unstructured scatter at every lag from $1$ to $9$
(correlation between lag and mean deviation over lags $1$--$9$: $-0.04$).

Consistently, dropping the adjacent years moves the pooled estimate by $1.8\%$ in Box B and $10.8\%$
in Box A, both *toward* zero rather than away — the opposite of attenuation. In Box A the $10.8\%$ is
on a small number and is within the noise.

This has a direct consequence for how the estimand should be described, taken up next.

# Caveats and concerns {#sec-caveats}

## The identification did not disappear; it moved into the estimand

This is the central qualification, and it should be read before any of the numbers are used.

$\widehat\Theta_k$ is unbiased for $\Theta_k$ **unconditionally** — that part of the claim is exactly
true, and it is a genuine improvement over identifying a target only under an assumption. But
$\Theta_k$ is defined as a contrast of mean footprints; calling it *the preferential sampling bias*
is a separate step, and that step needs

$$\big\langle \bar\delta^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k \big\rangle \;=\; 0,$$

i.e. that the *average* unaligned flow anomaly carries no alignment with year $k$'s field. That is
assumption (P) of the companion report, in a slightly weakened form — it need only hold on average
over the $M-1$ reference years, not year by year. It is weaker, it is testable in the same way, and
@sec-contamination finds no evidence against it. It is not absent.

The honest statement of what changed is therefore: **(P) has been demoted from an identification
condition to an interpretation condition.** Under the old framing, if (P) fails there is no
well-defined target and $T_k$ estimates nothing in particular. Under this one, $\widehat\Theta_k$
still estimates $\Theta_k$ exactly; what fails is only the claim that $\Theta_k$ *is* preferential
sampling. That is a real and useful separation — the estimate and its standard error survive
independently of the interpretive assumption, which is what makes reporting them defensible even
where the permutation test's assumptions are rejected. It is not the same as needing no assumption at
all, and the report should not be cited as though it were.

## The conservativeness claim is an assumption, not a theorem

It is tempting to argue that any residual memory in the reference must *attenuate* $\Theta_k$, so
that the estimand is conservative and the true preferential bias is larger. That argument is signed:
it presumes the contamination carries the same sign as the aligned pairing. Nothing in the
construction forces this — a lag-$1$ flow could as easily be anti-aligned with $\tilde Z_k$, in which
case the reference is deflated and $\Theta_k$ is *inflated*.

In these data the measured direction is the inflating one, weakly and insignificantly
(@sec-contamination). So "conservative" should be recorded as an assumption about the sign of ocean
memory that these ten years do not support, rather than as a property of the estimand. The defensible
statement is the two-sided one: the reference may be contaminated in either direction, the measured
contamination is consistent with zero, and dropping adjacent years moves the pooled estimate by less
than $2\%$ where it is large.

## What $\Theta_k$ cannot separate

- **Mechanism.** $\Theta_k$ cannot distinguish floats accumulating where the water is warm from
  floats and heat being redistributed together by the same eddies. Both satisfy $[S,X] \ne [S][X]$ in
  the sense of @diggle2010, and no design-based contrast will split them; that needs a model-based
  lens.
- **A preferential design from a merely non-representative one, in general.** The cancellation
  removes what is *common to all flow years*. A design feature that is non-representative and varies
  by flow year, but is unrelated to the field, enters $\delta^{(l)}$ and is removed only in
  expectation over the reference — it costs precision, and it is only the (P)-type condition that
  makes it cost no bias.
- **One realisation per year.** $\langle \delta^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$ is a single draw of the
  flow--field coupling. The ten analysis years are the replication, which is why the pooled row and
  the drift are the defensible statements and no individual year is. Doubling $D$ shrinks the Monte
  Carlo error but does not touch the between-year spread, which @tbl-pooled shows is the larger of
  the two in both boxes.
- **Two boxes.** Box B and Box A are matched on seeding law, margin, cadence, and over-density
  against real Argo, and differ in field amplitude ($3.3\times$), gradient, and current speed
  simultaneously. The pattern is consistent with the contrast requiring both a structured field and
  an energetic flow, but two boxes cannot attribute it to either.

## Inherited from the ensembles

These carry over unchanged from the companion report and are not repaired by the new framing.

- **Simulation, not observation.** GLORYS12 is a reanalysis; $\tilde Z$ is what remains after a
  parametric mean field is removed, and inherits whatever that fit left behind. $\Theta_k$ is a
  property of this simulated system.
- **Density.** Both virtual arrays run $2.4$--$2.6\times$ denser than the real Argo record over the
  same boxes. That leaves $\mathbb{E}[B]$ alone but narrows every sampling distribution, so the
  standard errors here are optimistic relative to a real-density array by roughly $\sqrt{2.5}$.
- **The seeding rectangle is not ocean-masked**, so about $3\%$ of Box B seeds land on land and never
  move. Those floats never enter $\hat Z$; the effect is a reduction in effective $n$, common to every
  flow year, and it cancels from $\Theta_k$ by the same argument as coverage bias.
- **$n$ is endogenous.** Retentive flow years hold more floats, so $\hat Z$ is a ratio estimator and
  the cells are matched only conditional on $n$. This is precisely the heteroscedasticity @tbl-var
  measures.

## Suggested change to the written method

Section 5 of the method draft bounds the pooled variance by $\max_k \operatorname{Var}
(\widehat\Theta_k)$, the worst case of perfect correlation, or proposes estimating it from replicate
subsamples. Neither is necessary: the per-draw unit statistic $U^{(l,d)}$ of the variance section
above gives the pooled variance in closed form, exactly and with no resampling, and the bound is
loose by $3.4$--$3.8\times$ in these data. The same construction yields the full covariance $\Sigma$,
without which the drift analysis is not available. The homoscedastic reduction should likewise be
demoted to a remark, since its premise is measurably false.
